name: GEF Small Grants Programme Turkmenistan
summary: Turkmenistan's GEF Small Grants country programme, run by CEPF, taking letters of inquiry from civil society organisations based in the country for community-based management of threatened ecosystems and species.

amount.note: Regular SGP grants; a lower limit may be set for individual calls

eligibility.rule: Registered in Turkmenistan, with a bank account in its name that takes foreign-currency wire transfers
If state-owned: legal personality independent of government, can receive private funds, no sovereign immunity
Implement no more than one SGP grant at a time during a GEF Operational Phase
Proposed activities target the Country Program Strategy priorities
No land purchase, physical resettlement, or adverse critical-habitat impacts

status.quote: The Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF) is currently accepting Letters of Inquiry (LOIs) from civil society organizations based in Turkmenistan for projects under the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Program (SGP).

amount.quote: Regular SGP grants have an upper limit of US$75,000, although a lower limit may be set for individual calls for proposals.

effort.quote: Turkmenistan Call for Letters of Inquiry for the GEF Small Grants Program Closes Tuesday, December 8, 2026.
All LOIs submitted will first be screened to confirm their eligibility. Eligible LOIs will then undergo preliminary technical review.
Following the recommendations of the NSC, organizations whose LOIs are selected will be invited to submit full project proposals.

eligibility.quote: Civil society organizations (CSOs) are eligible to receive an SGP grant if they: (a) are legally registered in the country in question; and (b) have a bank account in the organization’s name that can receive payments by wire transfer in foreign currency.

Government-owned enterprises or institutions are eligible only if they can establish: that the enterprise or institution has a legal personality independent of any government agency or actor, that the enterprise or institution has the authority to apply for and receive private funds in its own name and capacity, and that the enterprise or institution may not assert a claim of sovereign immunity.
Any given CSO is permitted to implement no more than one SGP grant at a time during a GEF Operational Phase.
Proposed activities must target the thematic and geographic priorities set out in the relevant Country Program Strategy.
Grants must not be used for the purchase of land, physical resettlement of people or activities that have the potential to cause adverse impacts to critical habitat.

after_award.quote: Milestones will be considered complete upon Grantee’s submission of the evidence of completion of the Milestone and CI’s verification of the acceptance criteria.
The Grantee shall submit a Final Completion and Impact Report within sixty (60) days following the end of the Grant Period.
